title: Gender-based differences in HIV detection and disease burden: a retrospective analysis of patients in a speciality clinic for infectious diseases in Berlin
summary: Despite constituting more than half of the people living with HIV worldwide, women and girls with HIV represent a minority in North America and Europe and have been historically under-represented in research and development into HIV treatment. Women living with HIV experience multifactorial stigma, potentially leading to delayed diagnosis, increased immune deficiency and morbidity compared to men. To our knowledge, no detailed gender study has been published on a German cohort. Demonstation of a gender gap in HIV care in Germany may help to raise awareness and improve the care of women living with HIV.

interventions.name: In a retrospective analysis, all patients aged ≥18 years with a new diagnosis of HIV who received care at the Clinic for Infecious Diseases of the Auguste-Viktoria-Klinikum, Berlin between the years of 2008-2025 will be included and anonymised.
